page: The Vultr voc-g-16c-64gb-320s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 16 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 8 physical cores on an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, supporting two threads per core. The hardware allocation includes 64.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per vCPU), 32 MB of L3 cache, and a bundled 320 GB local NVMe SSD. The processor features vector and cryptographic instruction sets, including AVX-512 (F, VNNI, and BF16), AES, and SHA-NI, without dedicated GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread and memory subsystem throughput. In stress-ng single-core tests, the instance registers in the top 10% with a score of 3,433.27, matched by a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3,056.57. Large-block memory bandwidth tests reach 286.47 GB/sec for uncached reads and 158.04 GB/sec for uncached writes, placing them in the top 25%. Geekbench single-core performance scores at 2,171.0, with text processing testing within the top 10%.

Multi-threaded computing and scale-out throughput settle into the middle 50% across standardized tests. Multi-core stress-ng yields 54,897.09, and Geekbench multi-core scores 15,790.0. Clang software compilation (29,072.0) and PassMark CPU ratings (40,911.05) remain solidly mid-tier. Small-model LLM generation (135M) achieves a strong 294.55 tokens/sec, while medium-model execution (7B) runs at 21.01 tokens/sec.

This hardware profile delivers a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, pairing dedicated AMD EPYC cores with high-speed local NVMe storage. Workloads best aligned with this configuration include relational databases, Redis in-memory caching (yielding 40.87 million SET ops/sec), continuous integration and compilation pipelines, and mid-tier backend web application services.
